key_insight: BiAlO3 is predicted to undergo a cubic-to-rhombohedral ferroelectric transition, with strong mode coupling governing its finite-temperature behavior.
engineering_relevance: As a lead-free perovskite ferroelectric, BiAlO3 offers a potentially high-polarization material platform for environmentally safer functional devices, but its properties are highly sensitive to temperature, pressure, and stress.
method: Finite-temperature simulation of structural, ferroelectric, and field-dependent behavior.
Evaluation of hydrostatic pressure and uniaxial/biaxial stress effects on phase stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative predictions of 81 μC/cm² room-temperature spontaneous polarization and a Curie temperature of 1160 K, consistent with an R3c ground state.
watch_item: The results are model-based predictions, so device deployment should account for possible discrepancies from real-material defects, strain conditions, and synthesis-dependent phase behavior.
paper_title: Atomistic study of finite temperature properties in ferroelectric BiAlO$_3$
